summary: Nauru is one of the hardest countries in the world to visit: there is no online portal, and most visitors must obtain a visa in advance from Nauru's immigration authorities, normally with confirmed flights and a hotel booking already in hand. Nauru's immigration regulations let nationals of a short list of countries — mostly Pacific neighbours such as Fiji, Kiribati and Papua New Guinea, plus China, Israel and Thailand — apply on arrival without a fee, and Russian and Spanish citizens need no visa.

fee.notes: Set by the Immigration Regulations 2014 (regulation 16): AUD 50 for a stay of up to 1 month, AUD 150 for up to 2 months and AUD 250 for up to 3 months. Payment must accompany the application (cash at the Nauru Revenue Office or a Nauruan consular post, or bank transfer) and is non-refundable.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could find states whether travel insurance is required to enter Nauru. The hospital handles only basic cases and evacuation means a flight to Brisbane, so cover with medical evacuation is worth having.

onwardTicket.text: Officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket, according to the Government of Canada's travel advice. No Nauruan official source we could find states the rule.

proofOfFunds.text: Under Nauru's Immigration Act, a person without sufficient lawful means of support for themselves and their dependants can be declared a prohibited immigrant, so be ready to show you can pay for your stay. No fixed amount is set.

declarations.name: Nauru arrival card
declarations.submitWindow: Completed on the aircraft or at Nauru International Airport on arrival
declarations.text: Every arriving passenger must complete and sign an arrival card — passport details, flight, intended address in Nauru, and for visitors the intended length of stay and main reason for the visit — and hand it to an immigration officer on request.

source.name: Immigration Act 2014 and Immigration Regulations 2014 (RONLAW, Republic of Nauru Online Legal Database)

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could find states Nauru's threshold for declaring cash. Nauru uses the Australian dollar and is largely a cash economy.

source.name: Republic of Nauru — government portal

notes: Quarantine rules are strict: fresh food, seeds, plants and animal products are generally prohibited.
Firearms, ammunition and offensive weapons require prior authorization and are otherwise banned.
Duty-free allowances for alcohol and tobacco are small and enforced. Declare anything above them.

payments.text: Nauru runs on Australian dollars in cash. Card acceptance is close to non-existent outside the main hotel, ATMs are unreliable or absent, and there is no way to withdraw money if you arrive empty-handed. Bring all the cash you will need.

safety.text: The crime rate is low, though petty crime such as pickpocketing and bag snatching can occur. Tourist facilities are extremely limited, medical facilities are limited and evacuation is expensive, beaches are unsupervised with strong currents and riptides, and there are no taxis or public transport.

source.name: Government of Canada — Nauru travel advice and advisories

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is drier and less humid. The November-to-February wet season brings heavy downpours, and the island is hot and humid all year.

tips.text: Start the visa process at least a month ahead. Applications are handled by email with Nauru's immigration office, responses can be slow, and unless your nationality is one of the few the regulations let apply on arrival there is nothing to fall back on — travelers are refused boarding without an approved visa.

Nauru Airlines is effectively the only way in, flying a handful of times a week from Brisbane and around the Pacific via Tarawa, Honiara, Majuro and Nadi. A missed flight can mean several extra days on the island.
Bring Australian dollars in cash for the whole trip. Assume no working ATM and no card payments.
Rooms are scarce — the Menen Hotel and a few guesthouses cover the whole island. Book and pay before applying for the visa, because the confirmation is part of the application.
Do not photograph government buildings, the airport, the port or the former asylum-seeker processing facilities, and ask before photographing people. Cameras have been confiscated for less.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Nauru?
faq.answer: For most nationalities, yes — including Australians, New Zealanders, Britons, Americans and most EU citizens, who must obtain a Nauru visa before arriving. There is no eVisa website; applications are made by email to Nauru's immigration authorities with your flight and accommodation bookings attached. The Immigration Regulations 2014 make two exceptions: nationals of Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, the Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, China, Israel and Thailand may apply for the visitor's visa on arrival and pay no fee, and Russian and Spanish citizens are exempt from the visa under visa waiver agreements.

faq.question: How do I apply for a Nauru tourist visa?
faq.answer: You request the application form from Nauru's immigration office, then return it with a passport copy, passport photo, confirmed Nauru Airlines flights, a paid hotel booking and a sponsor or itinerary. Allow two to four weeks. The fee is AUD 50 for a stay of up to one month (AUD 150 for two months, AUD 250 for three) and is paid with the application.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Nauru?
faq.answer: A visitor's visa can be granted for up to three months, single entry (Immigration Regulations 2014, regulation 12(7)), and the fee rises with the length: AUD 50 for one month, 150 for two and 250 for three. In practice the flight schedule sets the length of most visits. Extensions are possible through the immigration office on the island but should not be assumed.

faq.question: What currency does Nauru use and can I pay by card?
faq.answer: Nauru uses the Australian dollar and is a cash economy. Card acceptance is rare and ATMs cannot be relied on, so bring enough Australian dollars in cash to cover accommodation, food, transport and any fees.

faq.question: Is Nauru safe for visitors?
faq.answer: Generally, yes. Violent crime against visitors is rare, but the island has limited medical facilities, few emergency services and a serious road-accident risk on the ring road. Take out insurance with medical evacuation coverage and avoid alcohol-fueled situations at night.
